risks.note: India's Satcom sector is undergoing rapid policy evolution with ongoing discussions on spectrum assignment, usage charges and new authorizations. Management states the commercial ramp-up of LEO services is pending regulatory approvals and that this delay is directly impacting growth across multiple segments, deferring hybrid GEO-LEO deployments and associated equipment sales. The Company mitigates through continuous engagement with regulators and industry associations to ensure market access.
risks.risk: Regulatory and policy dependence - LEO / spectrum authorisations

risks.note: Operations depend on critical physical and satellite infrastructure susceptible to natural disasters, power outages, cyber incidents or human error; an unforeseen satellite failure could affect service continuity until alternative transponder capacity is available. Resilience is built through access to multiple satellites, teleport redundancy and hybrid networks. The BRSR materiality table repeats this as a business-continuity risk carrying revenue loss, recovery cost and brand damage.
risks.risk: Critical satellite and ground infrastructure failure

risks.note: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has introduced fresh volatility into global logistics and component sourcing; while semiconductor shortages have eased, geopolitical tensions threaten the stability of critical electronics and specialised Satcom hardware - particularly critical given the sector's reliance on imported Satcom equipment. Management also flags that input costs are rising due to the geopolitical situation, exerting further pressure on margins. Mitigation is via strategic partnerships, diversified sourcing, inventory planning and strategic buffer stocks.
risks.risk: Supply chain and geopolitical exposure to imported Satcom hardware

risks.note: The entry of global players into the Indian market alongside established domestic entities is intensifying competition, in a business where the Company currently holds a dominant ~40%+ revenue share it must defend. The Company responds by exploring new use cases, markets and strategic partnerships.

Rapid evolution in Satcom technologies creates challenges of adoption and obsolescence; the AR explicitly states that migration to newer systems involves cost and transitional complexity which may temporarily impact margins. Mitigated by investment in scalable, interoperable systems and long-term OEM partnerships.

Demand for satellite services is influenced by macroeconomic trends, availability of alternate technologies, government spending and sectoral shifts, and fluctuations in key verticals could affect short-term revenue and profitability. The AR also notes select segments are undergoing natural lifecycle contractions and that legacy equipment revenue streams are stagnant or declining; the Company is developing new segments to reduce dependency on a few markets.

As a satellite communication operator, data breaches and cyber-attacks could expose the Company to significant financial and reputational loss. Controls cited include ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, periodic VAPT and security audits, real-time threat monitoring, role-based access and encryption, third-party/vendor security assessment, and an FY2025-26 expansion of the internal audit scope to cover cybersecurity and cyber-financial risks. The Company states it has reinforced its resilience framework with advanced encryption and redundant network paths to ensure 99.9% uptime.

Forex exposures are monitored through board-approved hedging strategies with net positions kept within defined risk thresholds - structurally relevant because BRSR Section A reports 31.05% of turnover as revenue generated by providing services to customers located outside India, alongside imported equipment sourcing.
risks.risk: Foreign currency exposure and offshore revenue concentration

The Directors' Report states that the Company continuously evaluates opportunities for investment and augmentation of its technology, satellite network capabilities and ground infrastructure, and for developing new products and services to enable ubiquitous, reliable, secure and high-quality Satcom connectivity. Under its FY2026-27 strategic priorities the Company intends to strengthen gateway, teleport and network redundancy capabilities so as to support multi-orbit (GSO and NGSO) operations and deliver the very high uptime required by mission-critical customers, and to prepare networks and systems for multi-orbit and next-generation service models (Future Readiness). Capital allocation is described as disciplined - investing in infrastructure, partnerships and capabilities that offer sustainable returns and strategic relevance - and the MD notes the Company is investing in advanced technologies and building newer solutions. The single largest expansion lever is the accelerated roll-out of LEO services and hybrid GEO-LEO offerings, which remain pending regulatory approvals in India; no rupee quantum, timeline or named project is attached to any of these. The Board also confirmed that no material changes and commitments occurred after the close of the year that affect the financial position of the Company.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
